learn.hook: Kites in the Makar Sankranti sky, carrom boards and window panes are all quadrilaterals, but they belong to different branches of one big family!
points: A quadrilateral has 4 sides, 4 angles, 4 vertices and 2 diagonals. Its interior angles always add up to 360°, because a diagonal splits it into two triangles.
Trapezium: a pair of opposite sides parallel. Parallelogram: both pairs of opposite sides parallel.
Rectangle: a parallelogram with all angles 90°. Rhombus: a parallelogram with all sides equal. Square: both a rectangle and a rhombus.
Kite: two pairs of equal adjacent sides; its diagonals are perpendicular.
So every square is a rectangle and a rhombus, and every rectangle and rhombus is a parallelogram, but not the other way round.

example.q: The angles of a quadrilateral are x, x + 10°, x + 20° and x + 30°. Find all four angles.

learn.reallife: Engineers use parallelogram shapes in car jacks and folding gates, because they can change shape while opposite sides stay parallel.

games.title: Family facts
items: A square has all four sides equal, which is what a rhombus needs.
A rhombus can have angles like 60° and 120°, so it need not be a square.
A rectangle has both pairs of opposite sides parallel.
Both pairs of opposite sides of a square are parallel.
The angles of any quadrilateral add up to 180°
They add up to 360°: a diagonal makes two triangles of 180° each.
The diagonals of a kite are perpendicular
The long diagonal of a kite is a line of symmetry that cuts the other diagonal at right angles.

games.title: Name the quadrilateral
pairs: Both pairs of opposite sides parallel
Two pairs of equal adjacent sides

quiz.q: Three angles of a quadrilateral are 80°, 95° and 110°. What is the fourth angle?
quiz.explain: The angles add up to 360°, so the fourth angle is 360° − (80° + 95° + 110°) = 360° − 285° = 75°.
quiz.mistake: Uses 180° or makes an addition slip

quiz.q: The angles of a quadrilateral are in the ratio 1 : 2 : 3 : 4. What is the largest angle?
quiz.explain: There are 1 + 2 + 3 + 4 = 10 parts, so one part is 36°. The largest angle is 4 × 36° = 144°.
quiz.mistake: Divides 180° instead of 360° into the parts, getting 72°

quiz.q: Which statement is always true?
quiz.explain: A square has four equal sides, so it is a special rhombus. The others are true only sometimes.
quiz.mistake: Reverses the family tree: a square is a rhombus, but a rhombus need not be a square

quiz.q: A quadrilateral has exactly one pair of parallel sides. What is it?
quiz.explain: A quadrilateral with only one pair of parallel sides is a trapezium. Parallelograms and rhombuses have two pairs.
quiz.mistake: Thinks any shape with parallel sides is a parallelogram

quiz.q: Which quadrilateral has two pairs of equal adjacent sides and diagonals that cross at right angles, but need not have parallel sides?
quiz.explain: That is a kite, like the ones flown on Makar Sankranti.
quiz.mistake: Confuses a kite with a rhombus or parallelogram

quiz.q: A rhombus has equal diagonals. What special quadrilateral is it?
quiz.explain: A parallelogram with equal diagonals is a rectangle. A rhombus that is also a rectangle is a square.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the diagonals of a rhombus can never be equal

quiz.q: What is the sum of the exterior angles of a convex quadrilateral, taking one at each vertex?
quiz.explain: Walking once round any convex polygon you turn through one full turn, 360°.
quiz.mistake: Confuses exterior angles with the sum of interior angles of a triangle

quiz.q: The angles of a quadrilateral are x, x + 10°, x + 20° and x + 30°. What is the largest angle?
quiz.explain: 4x + 60° = 360°, so x = 75°. The largest angle is x + 30° = 105°.
quiz.mistake: Gives x (75°) instead of the largest angle

teach.ask: Gappu is puzzled: "My teacher says a square is a rectangle. But they have different names! How can that be?"
teach.praise: A rectangle just needs four right angles and opposite sides equal and parallel. A square has all that, so it is a special kind of rectangle!
teach.nudge: What does a shape need to be called a rectangle? Does a square have those things?

learn.hook: Push the top of a folding gate sideways: it leans, but opposite sides stay equal and parallel. That's the parallelogram's superpower!
points: A diagonal divides a parallelogram into two congruent triangles.
In a parallelogram, opposite sides are equal and opposite angles are equal.
Adjacent angles are supplementary: they add up to 180° (co-interior angles between parallel lines).
The diagonals bisect each other: they cut each other into two equal halves.

A quadrilateral is a parallelogram if any one of these holds: both pairs of opposite sides equal, both pairs of opposite angles equal, diagonals bisect each other, or one pair of opposite sides is both equal and parallel. In a rectangle the diagonals are also equal; in a rhombus they are also perpendicular.

example.q: In parallelogram PQRS, ∠P = 65°. Find the other three angles.

learn.reallife: Table lamps with folding arms, the scissor lift used by electricians and many bridge frames rely on parallelogram properties.

items.text: Opposite angles of a parallelogram are ___
Adjacent angles of a parallelogram add up to ___
The diagonals of a parallelogram ___ each other
The diagonals of a rhombus cross at ___
The diagonals of a rectangle are ___

quiz.q: One angle of a parallelogram is 70°. What is the size of an angle next to it?
quiz.explain: Adjacent angles of a parallelogram are supplementary: 180° − 70° = 110°.
quiz.mistake: Thinks all angles of a parallelogram are equal, or subtracts from 90°

quiz.q: In parallelogram ABCD the diagonals meet at O, and AC = 16 cm. What is AO?
quiz.explain: The diagonals of a parallelogram bisect each other, so AO = 16 ÷ 2 = 8 cm.
quiz.mistake: Forgets that bisect means cut into two equal halves

quiz.q: A parallelogram has sides 9 cm and 6 cm. What is its perimeter?
quiz.explain: Opposite sides are equal, so the perimeter is 2 × (9 + 6) = 30 cm.
quiz.mistake: Adds only two sides, or multiplies the sides

quiz.q: Two opposite angles of a parallelogram are (3x − 10)° and (2x + 20)°. What is the size of each of these angles?
quiz.explain: Opposite angles are equal: 3x − 10 = 2x + 20, so x = 30. Each angle is 3 × 30 − 10 = 80°.
quiz.mistake: Gives x (30) as the angle, or uses supplementary angles by mistake

quiz.q: Which of these is NOT always true for a parallelogram?
quiz.explain: Equal diagonals happen only when the parallelogram is a rectangle (or square).
quiz.mistake: Assumes rectangle properties hold for every parallelogram

quiz.q: The diagonals of a rhombus are 12 cm and 16 cm. What is the length of each side?
quiz.explain: The diagonals bisect each other at right angles, making right triangles with legs 6 cm and 8 cm. Side = √(36 + 64) = 10 cm.
quiz.mistake: Uses the whole diagonals instead of their halves, getting 20 cm

quiz.q: Which condition guarantees that a quadrilateral is a parallelogram?
options: One pair of opposite sides is equal
One pair of opposite sides is both equal and parallel
quiz.explain: If one pair of opposite sides is equal AND parallel, the quadrilateral must be a parallelogram. Just equal is not enough: an isosceles trapezium has one pair of equal opposite sides.
quiz.mistake: Thinks one pair of equal sides is enough

quiz.q: Two adjacent angles of a parallelogram are in the ratio 2 : 3. What is the smaller angle?
quiz.explain: Adjacent angles add to 180°. 180° ÷ 5 = 36°, so the angles are 72° and 108°.
quiz.mistake: Divides 360° into the parts as if they were all four angles

teach.ask: Gappu draws a slanted four-sided shape: "How can I be sure this is a parallelogram, and what do I get for free if it is?"
teach.praise: If both pairs of opposite sides are parallel, then opposite sides and angles are equal, and the diagonals bisect each other. So many free facts!
teach.nudge: What can you say about the opposite sides? And what happens where the diagonals cross?

learn.hook: Join the middles of two sides of any triangle and something magical appears: a line exactly parallel to the third side and exactly half as long!
points: Mid-point theorem: the segment joining the mid-points of two sides of a triangle is parallel to the third side and is half of it.
If D and E are mid-points of AB and AC in triangle ABC, then DE ∥ BC and DE = ½ BC.
Converse: a line through the mid-point of one side of a triangle, parallel to another side, bisects the third side.
Joining the mid-points of the three sides makes 4 congruent triangles, each with ¼ of the area of the original.
Joining the mid-points of the sides of ANY quadrilateral, in order, always gives a parallelogram.

example.q: In triangle ABC, AB = 8 cm, BC = 10 cm and CA = 12 cm. D, E and F are the mid-points of AB, BC and CA. Find the perimeter of triangle DEF.
steps: By the mid-point theorem, each side of DEF is half of a side of ABC
DE = ½ CA = 6, EF = ½ AB = 4, FD = ½ BC = 5

learn.reallife: Carpenters use the mid-point idea to fix a cross-bar exactly halfway up a triangular roof frame, knowing it will be level and half the width of the base.

games.title: Prove the mid-point theorem
games.prompt: D, E are mid-points of AB, AC. Put the proof in order.
items: Extend DE to F so that EF = DE, and join CF
Triangles ADE and CFE are congruent (SAS), so CF = AD = DB and CF ∥ AB
Hence DF ∥ BC and DF = BC
Since DE = ½ DF, DE = ½ BC and DE ∥ BC

items.q: BC = 18 cm. Length of DE joining mid-points of AB and AC (cm)?
Triangle perimeter 40 cm. Perimeter of mid-point triangle (cm)?
Triangle area 64 cm². Area of mid-point triangle (cm²)?
Number of congruent triangles formed by joining all three mid-points

quiz.q: In triangle ABC, D and E are the mid-points of AB and AC, and BC = 14 cm. What is DE?
quiz.explain: By the mid-point theorem, DE = ½ BC = 7 cm.
quiz.mistake: Doubles instead of halving

quiz.q: D and E are the mid-points of AB and AC of triangle ABC. If DE = 4.5 cm, what is BC?
quiz.explain: DE is half of BC, so BC = 2 × 4.5 = 9 cm.
quiz.mistake: Halves DE again instead of doubling it

quiz.q: A triangle has sides 8 cm, 10 cm and 12 cm. What is the perimeter of the triangle formed by joining the mid-points of its sides?
quiz.explain: Each side of the new triangle is half of a side of the old one, so its perimeter is ½ × 30 = 15 cm.
quiz.mistake: Gives the original perimeter

quiz.q: D and E are the mid-points of AB and AC in triangle ABC. DE is parallel to which side?
quiz.explain: The segment joining the mid-points of two sides is parallel to the third side, BC.
quiz.mistake: Thinks DE is parallel to one of the sides it touches

quiz.q: In triangle ABC, a line through the mid-point of AB is drawn parallel to BC. Where does it meet AC?
options: One-third of the way from A
quiz.explain: By the converse of the mid-point theorem, the line bisects AC.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the meeting point depends on the triangle's shape

quiz.q: Aisha joins the mid-points of the sides of an irregular quadrilateral, in order. What shape does she always get?
quiz.explain: Each pair of opposite sides of the new shape is parallel to (and half of) the same diagonal, so it is always a parallelogram.
quiz.mistake: Expects a square because the shape looks neat

quiz.q: The diagonals of a rectangle are 10 cm long. What is the perimeter of the quadrilateral formed by joining the mid-points of its sides?
quiz.explain: Each side of the new shape is half of a diagonal, so each side is 5 cm. It is a rhombus with perimeter 4 × 5 = 20 cm.
quiz.mistake: Uses the full diagonal as each side, getting 40 cm

quiz.q: A triangle has area 48 cm². What is the area of the triangle formed by joining the mid-points of its three sides?
quiz.explain: Joining the mid-points makes 4 congruent triangles, so the middle one has ¼ of the area: 48 ÷ 4 = 12 cm².
quiz.mistake: Halves the area because the sides are halved

teach.ask: Gappu joins the middles of two sides of a triangle with a straw: "Is there anything special about this straw?"
teach.praise: It is parallel to the third side and exactly half its length. That's the mid-point theorem! My straw is famous.
teach.nudge: Compare the straw with the third side. Which way does it point, and how long is it?
